atoms.b: Emilio grew up in St Ives in Cornwall and spent many summers on the beach. From a young age, Emilio was fascinated by ((++marine)) life. As a child, Emilio ((++absorbed)) as much information about the ocean as possible. His favourite birthday was his fourteenth, when his parents gifted him a pair of ((++goggles)) and a snorkelling tour with his dad.

Ever since he was little, he knew that he wanted to be a marine biologist. Emilio’s absolute favourite animal is the swordfish, especially since he finds the strength of the swordfish to be unique and ((++breathtaking)). When he was older, Emilio found a course that was a ((++collaboration)) with the University of Exeter and a wildlife conservation program, to work with swordfish in their natural habitat. When he looked at the application deadline, he realised it was the next day and ((++frantically)) finished his application in one evening.
A few months later, Emilio received a letter in the post, informing him that he had been accepted into the course! The course was a ((++hybrid)), half in the classroom and half in the sea.

atoms.b: Three weeks later and Emilio was out in the field! Emilio held on to his hat as he felt the boat he was on ((++speed_up --slow_down)). It was his third week into the course, and now his team was on its way to the annual swordfish migration. He heard the captain quietly ((++muttering --yelling)) about their expected arrival to one of his teammates and could barely contain himself. Emilio carefully ((++extracted --threw_out)) his camera from his wet jacket when he heard a sudden explosive splash.

It was an enormous swordfish, perhaps 8 feet long. It looked even more ((++majestic)) than anything he had seen in books or online before. His teammates ((++frantically --ruggedly)) hurried over, each trying to get the best view. As quickly as it had appeared, it disappeared. “That was just one of many ((++breathtaking)) shots, wait until we’re even closer”, he heard his boss excitedly whisper to him.
